In [[mathematics]], '''Sierpiński's theorem''' is an isomorphism theorem concerning certain [[metric space]]s, named after [[Wacław Sierpiński]] who proved it in 1920.{{r|sierpiński}}

It states that any [[countable]] [[metric space]] without [[isolated point]]s is [[homeomorphic]] to <math>\mathbb{Q}</math> (with its standard topology).{{r|sierpiński|błaszczyk|dasgupta|engelking|kechris|van-mill}}

==Examples==

As a consequence of the theorem, the metric space <math>\mathbb{Q}^2</math> (with its usual [[Euclidean distance]]) is homeomorphic to <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>, which may seem counterintuitive. This is in contrast to, e.g., <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math>, which is not homeomorphic to <math>\mathbb{R}</math>. As another example, <math>\mathbb{Q} \cap [0, 1]</math> is also homeomorphic to <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>, again in contrast to the closed real interval <math>[0, 1]</math>, which is not homeomorphic to <math>\mathbb{R}</math> (whereas the open interval <math>(0, 1)</math> is).
